title: Bottom-pinned transcript oscillates and typing lags when a Mermaid diagram is resident
outcome:
Symptoms (Greg, 2026-08-25, slower laptop, idle sessions, low CPU): (1) prompt composer typing feels laggy; (2) transcript pinned at the bottom bobs up/down by a few pixels; (3) suspected Mermaid involvement. All three share one root cause hypothesis, code-derived (not yet profiled on the affected machine).

ROOT CAUSE (feedback loop): Mermaid diagrams render in an iframe sized by getMermaidDiagramFrameStyle (ui/src/mermaid-render.ts:202-240) with width:Wpx; max-width:100%; height:auto; aspect-ratio:W/H - so the iframe's RENDERED HEIGHT is a linear function of the message-stack column width. The .message-stack (ui/src/styles.css:4467) has overflow:auto and NO scrollbar-gutter:stable (the only stable-gutter rules are on composer slash palettes, :9558/:9644), so scrollbar appearance changes content width by ~17px on Windows. Loop: scrollbar appears -> column narrows -> width-constrained diagram gets proportionally shorter -> total scrollHeight drops below the overflow threshold -> scrollbar disappears -> column widens -> diagram taller -> scrollbar reappears. Each flip changes the conversation page height by more than the 0.5px threshold in repinAfterRelevantResize (ui/src/SessionPaneView.scroll.ts:728-762, ResizeObserver on conversation page + pane frame), which while tail-pinned calls scrollToLatestMessage synchronously -> layout + scroll write + virtualizer bottom_follow handling + possible page-height commits (virtualized-conversation-page-heights.ts) -> more layout. Browsers break ResizeObserver loops per frame, so the cycle spreads across frames: visually a few-pixel bob, average CPU low, but continuous per-frame main-thread layout work - typing events queue behind it, producing composer lag on slow hardware. An independent second trigger with the same loop shape: fractional-pixel rounding of the aspect-ratio height under display scaling (125/150 percent) can alternate between two rounded heights even without a scrollbar flip. The composer input path itself was audited and is lean (uncontrolled textarea, no-op state for non-slash drafts, rAF-batched resize with a prior lag fix documented at useComposerAutoResize.ts:238-243) - it is not the lag source.

SUPPORTING DETAIL: mermaid-render.ts:167-177 already documents that rendered height can differ by a couple of pixels from the viewBox-derived frame; MermaidDiagram (ui/src/markdown-content.tsx:68-199) renders once per [appearance, code] with memoized srcDoc, so React re-render churn is ruled out; the loading-placeholder -> iframe swap also causes a one-time height jump per virtualizer mount (minor, tab-switch estimate churn).

SUGGESTED FIX (two small, independent layers):
F1 scrollbar decoupling: add scrollbar-gutter:stable to .message-stack (one line) - eliminates the scrollbar-width flip for every width-sensitive card, not just Mermaid. Visual cost: a permanently reserved gutter; note the overview-rail mode already hides the native scrollbar (styles.css :has(.has-conversation-overview-scroll) scrollbar-width:none), so this only affects panes without the rail.
F2 repin hysteresis: in repinAfterRelevantResize, ignore content-height deltas at or below ~2px when NOT in live flow (liveFlowActiveRef false and no settled bottom-follow active) - a few-pixel measurement wobble must not trigger a bottom repin at all; the current threshold is 0.5px. This kills DPI-rounding oscillation independent of F1. Keep live-flow behavior byte-identical (streaming growth must still repin every pixel).
Optional F3: pin the mermaid iframe height to whole pixels after first settle (explicit px height instead of live aspect-ratio) if F1+F2 leave residual wobble.

VALIDATION PLAN: reproduce on the affected machine first - DevTools Performance overlay should show recurring ResizeObserver/layout activity while idle with a Mermaid message resident, and the bob should disappear when the Mermaid card is scrolled out of the render window or the diagram removed. Regression tests: (a) unit - repinAfterRelevantResize with a 2px content-height delta while idle-pinned performs no scroll write, while a 2px delta during live flow still repins; (b) existing scroll-behavior suites stay green (attached-follow thresholds unchanged in live flow); (c) manual/probe check on Windows-style classic scrollbars for the F1 gutter. Typing-lag symptom is expected to disappear with the loop; if residual lag remains on the slow laptop, profile the composer path separately (it is currently clean).
acceptance:
1. With a Mermaid diagram resident in a bottom-pinned transcript and sessions idle, the viewport performs zero scroll writes and zero ResizeObserver-driven repins over an extended observation window: no few-pixel bobbing, no cursor-shape flicker over stationary text, on both standard and 125/150 percent display scaling and with classic (width-consuming) scrollbars.
2. Composer typing latency on slow hardware returns to parity with panes that contain no Mermaid content; the composer input path itself remains unchanged (uncontrolled textarea, rAF-batched resize).
3. Live-flow behavior is byte-identical: during streaming/attached follow, every real content growth still repins immediately (no hysteresis applies while liveFlowActiveRef or a settled bottom-follow is active).
4. Focused regression: repinAfterRelevantResize ignores idle content-height deltas at or below the hysteresis threshold (~2px) while tail-pinned and NOT in live flow, and still repins for the same delta during live flow; existing App.scroll-behavior and virtualization suites stay green.
5. Scrollbar decoupling verified: .message-stack reserves gutter space (scrollbar-gutter: stable) so scrollbar appearance no longer changes content width; overview-rail panes (scrollbar-width: none) are unaffected.
6. Manual confirmation on the affected laptop: pointer held still over transcript text with a Mermaid message visible keeps a stable cursor shape; DevTools Performance shows no recurring layout/RO activity while idle.
7. UI gates pass: cd ui && npx tsc --noEmit clean, npx vitest run green.
